title: feat(objectql, plugin-approvals): assignment rules and approval steps read the queue they name from their declaring package (ADR-0150 D3)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi98A9RbunRmd8Yo27MCdemFr)_

Fixes #31790

Clause-②: yes (widening); narrowing per ADR-0150 D3 declared below
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: follow-up owed, filed as #31853 (domain:skills, blocked by #31790) — skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md (Assignment rules: a declared rule's queue is read from its package, else a declared dependency's) and skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md (Approver Types: a `queue` approver likewise, from the flow's package). The sharing-rule half is already taught in skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md.
Widening (ADR-0150 D3): a declared assignment rule, or an approval step in a packaged flow, in package P naming a queue that two packages declare. Before (main `fdfcc7ab`): refused `ambiguous-in-environment`. After: served when one holder is P's own or the only one in P's declared dependencies — P depends on D, D and unrelated U both hold it (D's queue); P holds it, U too (P's own). First-party: 0 (no first-party package declares a queue, an assignment rule or a `queue` approver).
Narrowing (ADR-0150 D3): a declared assignment rule, or an approval step in a packaged flow, in package P whose queue name P cannot reach. Before (main `fdfcc7ab`): served environment-wide. After: refused `outside-closure`, naming every candidate. Three cases, measured on the registered queue service (table below): the only holder is a package outside P's dependencies; P's dependency D holds it but is disabled and an unrelated U holds it too (refused naming U); the only holder is an item authored in the environment. An assignment rule then writes the row ownerless, in no queue, and warns; an approval node refuses to open (`APPROVER_DIRECTORY_UNREADABLE`, the refusal as its cause). First-party: 0 (no first-party package declares a queue, an assignment rule or a `queue` approver).
Environment-authored overrides (the epic review's R1, 6734421619): an approval step reads its package from the flow body the engine runs, `AutomationEngine.armedFlowPackage` (#31863). An environment-authored `.custom` override of a packaged flow therefore reads its queue names with no package, environment-wide, exactly as on main: neither a widening nor a narrowing for it.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：软件包里声明的「分配规则」和流程里的「审批步骤」引用队列名时，现在把声明它的软件包（规则所在的包、流程所在的包）交给队列服务，队列从这个包出发解析：本包的队列，否则它声明依赖的包里唯一的持有者，否则拒绝并列出全部候选。组织自己建的分配规则、不属于任何包的规则和流程，照旧按整个环境查。
- 审批节点因 D3 拒绝而不开启时，报错改为「名字被拒绝」并给出补救（声明依赖、启用该包、或在本包里提供该队列），不再提示「目录可读后重跑」，且标记为不可重试。
- 环境里对包流程做的 `.custom` 覆盖：审批步骤按引擎实际运行的那份定义取包（`armedFlowPackage`，来自 #31863），覆盖的步骤按「无包」查，与 main 一致（史诗评审 R1）。
- 为什么改：#31789 给队列服务契约加了「调用方软件包」参数，但只有共享规则在用。这两处还按整个环境查，所以「规则依赖的包和一个无关包都有同名队列」会被拒绝，比 ADR-0150 D3 更严（专题 #31527）。
- 风险与回滚：只影响「包里的规则或审批步骤引用队列，且队列名有多个持有者或持有者不在依赖里」的部署。第一方实测 0 个包声明队列、分配规则或队列审批人。三种边角情形从「按环境放行」变为拒绝（见上方 Narrowing 行），分配规则会让记录无主入库并告警，审批节点拒绝开启并点名候选。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts` 的 `route`（`fromPackage` 两处调用）；`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` 的 `flowPackageOf` 与 `expandQueueUsers`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run src/approval-service.test.ts -t "ADR-0150 D3"`，预期 7 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地（R1 部分等 #31863）。

## What changes

- **Assignment rules (`@objectstack/objectql`, `assignment-rules.ts`).** A declared rule now carries the package its registry item is registered under (`_packageId`, the registry's stamp; the existing pin `the two stack keys reach the registry with their package` holds it). `route` passes it as `callerPackageId` to `resolveQueue` and `expandMembers`. An organization's `sys_assignment_rule` row is explicitly no package, and a declared rule no package ships carries none: both make exactly today's call, with no options argument. The "does not resolve" warning names the rule's package when there is one. Module doc gains a "Which queue a name means" section.
- **Approval steps (`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `approval-service.ts`).** A step's package is the package of the flow body the engine runs: `flowPackageOf(flowName)` asks the automation engine's public `armedFlowPackage` (#31863), the reader the engine's own subflow addressing (ADR-0150 E1) takes a run's caller package from. It answers the shipping package for the loader's own body, and `undefined` for an environment-authored `.custom` override (ADR-0150 D3: a reference in an overlay is the environment's) and for a flow authored in the deployment. `ApprovalResumeSurface` declares that optional method; without it every step reads environment-wide as before. ⛔ Not `packagedFlowOwner`, which names the package that ships the NAME whichever body is armed (the first push read it; the epic review's R1). `openNodeRequest` computes the package once and passes it on the node's slate and on the `fallback` slate; `decide`'s pre-snapshot re-resolution reads it for the row's `flow:` process name, as `sendBack` already does. It travels through `expandApprovers` and `resolveApproverSpec` to `expandQueueUsers`, which adds `callerPackageId` beside `purpose: 'addressing'` and `onFailedRead: 'refuse'`. A deployment-authored flow and an override make today's call unchanged.
- **A refused queue name on an approval node.** The node still refuses with `ApproverDirectoryUnreadableError` (`APPROVER_DIRECTORY_UNREADABLE`), the refusal as its cause, and still routes past no one. When the cause is a D3 refusal (read by its shape, `refusal.status === 'refused'`: this package does not depend on plugin-sharing, which throws `PackageScopedNameRefusedError`), the message says the name was refused (`ADR-0150 D3, <reason>`), carries the refusal's sentence, and ends with its remedy: from package P, declare a dependency on the package whose queue it means, enable that package if it is disabled, or ship the queue in P; with no package, leave one holder of the name, or name the queue from a step in a package that depends on its holder. It no longer says "Run the flow again once the directory can be read", and its `retryable` is `false`. A failed read keeps its wording, byte for byte, and `retryable: true`. No new code: reworded under the existing one (epic review R2).
- ⛔ No second resolver and no first-registered fallback: both readers only name the package; the queue service (`IOwnershipQueueService`, implemented by plugin-sharing over objectql's `resolvePackageScopedName`) decides.
- Changeset: patch for `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, with both declaration lines and the narrowing.

## Step 0: how each reader learns its declaring package

Measured on `origin/main` `fdfcc7ab` (with #31789).

| Reader | Where the name is written | Package coordinate | After this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| objectql assignment seam, declared rule | `assignmentRules` item, `host.listRules()` = `registry.listItems('assignment_rule')` | the item's `_packageId` (stamped by `registerItem` / `applyProtection`; already pinned in `ownership-queue.test.ts`) | passed |
| objectql assignment seam, organization rule | `sys_assignment_rule` row | none (an organization's row) | not passed: environment-wide |
| plugin-approvals approver slate (`queue` approver) | approval node config inside a flow; `openNodeRequest` gets `flowName` from the engine-seeded `$flowName` | `AutomationEngine.armedFlowPackage(flowName)` (#31863: the package whose own body is armed; `undefined` for an override or a deployment-authored flow) | passed when the armed body is a package's own |
| plugin-approvals `decide` pre-snapshot tally | stored request row | the row's `process_name` (`flow:NAME`) to `armedFlowPackage` | passed when the armed body is a package's own |

The definition's own `_packageId` is deliberately not read for flows: the engine documents it as the caller's bytes, and an override's served copy carries the base's. Both readers have a coordinate, so no stop.

## Tests

objectql, new top-level `describe` in the D5 harness `src/ownership-queue.test.ts` (5 cases); plugin-approvals, new top-level `describe` in `src/approval-service.test.ts` (7 cases). Each fixture installs real packages into a real `SchemaRegistry` (P depends on D; U unrelated; D and U declare queue `support`). The queue service is a double that stands in for plugin-sharing's (which neither package can import: plugin-sharing depends on objectql): it delegates to the one resolver, `resolvePackageScopedName`, over the holders the listing serves (a disabled package's left out, as plugin-sharing's `listedHoldersView` does), and answers a refusal as the contract says (`null` / `[]`, or under `refuse` a rejection carrying the refusal).

| Pin | objectql | plugin-approvals |
|:--|:--|:--|
| P's rule/step naming `support`, held by D and U, reaches D's queue | **red on main** | **red on main** |
| two holders in P's closure: refused, naming both | **red on main** | **red on main** |
| D disabled + U: refused `outside-closure`, naming U, U never served | **red on main** | **red on main** |
| CONTROL: no package (a declared rule no package ships / a deployment-authored flow) reads as today, same call, same refusal | green on main | green on main |
| CONTROL (objectql): an organization's own rule reads environment-wide | green on main | — |
| fallback slate and pre-snapshot tally read the same package (plugin-approvals) | — | **red on main** |
| a D3 refusal on the node reads as a refusal with its remedy, not retryable (asserted in the two-in-closure pin and the CONTROL) | — | **red on main** (failed-read wording) |
| an environment-authored override of P's flow (`armedFlowPackage` undefined, `packagedFlowOwner` P) naming an environment-held queue P cannot reach: served environment-wide, on the node slate and the pre-snapshot tally | — | green on main; **red with `packagedFlowOwner`** (refused `outside-closure`) |
| the same on the override's `fallback` slate | — | green on main; **red with `packagedFlowOwner`** |

"Red on main" was measured by restoring the two source files to `fdfcc7ab` (`git restore --source`), running the blocks, and restoring (`git diff HEAD` empty): objectql 3 of 5 red, plugin-approvals 4 of 5 red, every CONTROL green.

Forced test-infrastructure change: `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/vitest.config.ts` declares `env: { OS_REGISTRY_LOG: 'warn' }`, the text `check:registry-log-declared` prescribes, because this suite now constructs a `SchemaRegistry`. No existing test was edited.

## Acceptance notes

- **Widening, declared beside the narrowing.** Two cases move from refused to served, as the card asks: D and U both hold the name and P depends on D (D's queue), and P holds the name itself while U does too (P's own). Declared `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, as #31789 declared the same movement (seat ruling; claim amended on the card, 6734711604), with the narrowing stated beside it. Accepted by the epic review (6734421619).
- **The package of a flow step is `armedFlowPackage`, one reader.** #31863 added it for every caller (E1's subflow addressing, E5's connector_action, this step). An R1 first cut built a reader here before #31863 existed; it was withdrawn on the seat's instruction (`fe45524b`) and never reached main. This PR only reads #31863's.
- **An assignment rule never sees the candidates.** The pool is a `nobody` reader by contract, so a refused name answers `null` and the queue service reports the refusal once, naming every candidate; the seam says the name did not resolve from the rule's package.
- **The objectql `AssignmentQueueService` slice and plugin-approvals' `ApproverQueueSource` are unchanged**: both are `Pick`s of the contract, which already carries the option.

## Verification

Head `00fb75d5`. It merges `origin/main` at `5d17aa6b`, which includes #31863's `armedFlowPackage`, through merge commit `f3864c02`. The first push was `0dccea6c`.
- `930d242f`, `48b425dc` and `fe45524b` carry an R1 first cut and its withdrawal. Net, they leave `packages/services/**` identical to main.
- `00fb75d5` switches the approval step to #31863's reader.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test` (under the lock, on `00fb75d5`): Test Files 115 passed (115), Tests 1509 passed (1509). The new block is 7/7.
- Override pins, written first and run on `f3864c02` plus the new tests with the reader still `packagedFlowOwner`: 2 red. After the switch: green.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test` (under the lock, on `fd340a92`; this PR's objectql files have not changed since): Test Files 579 passed (579), Tests 11868 passed (11868).
- `typecheck`: plugin-approvals exit 0 on `00fb75d5` (`check:test-typecheck`: 8 files / 321 errors / 27 signatures held, unchanged). objectql exit 0 at the first push.
- Lint: neither package has a `lint` script. Root `npx eslint --no-inline-config packages/objectql/src packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src` exits 0 on `00fb75d5`.
- `dispatch-gates --ran` on `00fb75d5`, on a clean tree: 74 derived, 74 run, every one recorded `exit 0`, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- Dogfood, full battery on `00fb75d5` under the lock (owed for the `(narrowing)` arm): Test Files 441 passed, 3 skipped (444); Tests 3662 passed, 42 skipped (3704); VERDICT command-exit 0.

<details><summary>Measured: what the registered queue service answers, environment-wide (main's readers) and from P (this PR's)</summary>

A throwaway test (deleted, never committed) drove `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`'s `OwnershipQueueService` over a real `SchemaRegistry` on this tree. `resolveQueue('support')`, and `expandMembers` under `refuse` from P:

| Case | environment-wide | from P | refuse from P |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| P depends on D; D and unrelated U hold it | null (refused) | D's queue | ok |
| two holders in P's closure | null (refused) | null | `ambiguous-in-closure` [D, D2] |
| only unrelated U holds it | **U's queue** | null | `outside-closure` [U] |
| D disabled; U holds it too | **U's queue** | null | `outside-closure` [U] |
| only an environment-declared item | **the environment's** | null | `outside-closure` [environment] |
| P holds it, U too | null (refused) | P's own | ok |
| only D holds it | D's | D's | ok |
| no declared holder, an organization's `sys_queue` row | the row | the row | ok |

The three bold rows are the narrowing; rows 1 and 6 the widening the card asks for.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations: six legs, each red, each restored (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs)</summary>

Both suites import their package's source directly; no dist leg. A1–A4 ran on `0dccea6c`; R2 on the head below. Each leg: anchor 1 to 0, blob changed, run red, restored with blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.

- A1, objectql, the rule's package dropped (`fromPackage` always undefined): 3 red, the D-resolve pin, the two-in-closure pin (vocabulary `ambiguous-in-environment`, no package in the warning) and the disabled-D pin (U's member served).
- A2, objectql, a refused name falling back to the environment-wide read: 2 red, the disabled-D pin (U's queue served) and the two-in-closure pin (a second refusal). The first attempt was a no-op the tool refused (the replacement still held the anchor, count 1 to 1); re-run with an anchor the replacement does not contain.
- A3, plugin-approvals, the flow's package dropped: 4 red, every package pin.
- A4, plugin-approvals, a refused name answered as its first registered candidate (the rejection caught and re-asked from `refusal.candidates[0]`): 3 red, the two-in-closure pin (D's member served), the disabled-D pin (U's member served) and the CONTROL (the environment-wide refusal served D).

- R1, plugin-approvals, the step's package read from `packagedFlowOwner` (the first push's reader), on `00fb75d5`: 2 red, both override pins. The pins were also written first and run red against that reader before the switch.
- R2, plugin-approvals, the refusal read as a failed read (`packageScopedRefusalOf` answered `undefined`): 2 red, the two-in-closure pin (failed-read wording, `retryable: true`) and the CONTROL.

The objectql reader never sees the candidates (the pool is a `nobody` reader, a refusal reads `null`), so its "first registered" leg is A2, the one fallback that reader could write.
</details>
